bounded_predicate: A constructor/call name in the fixed primitive-array table, first literal lambda argument, at most one body statement, and final expression text exactly a listed default value; report the whole call.

positive.intent: Numeric zero and Boolean false initialization exercise two default-value families without claiming a measured speedup.

sources.Case.kt:
package corpus.arrayinit

fun zeroValues(): IntArray = IntArray(4)
fun clearFlags(): BooleanArray = BooleanArray(2)
fun indexedValues(): IntArray = IntArray(4) { index -> index }

negative.intent: Default constructors retain default initialization; index-dependent initialization is genuinely useful and not a listed constant.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on the package-isolated copy. Preserve every positive range from the byte-identical unsuppressed neighbor. No host finding filter or ktChecker-ID suppression alias.

controls.intent: A mutable audit update before returning zero must survive. The real upstream multi-statement guard declines to recommend removing it.

sources.Case.kt:
package corpus.arrayinit

fun computedZeros(): IntArray = IntArray(4) { 1 - 1 }

controls.intent: A constant-valued arithmetic expression is not one of the exact default strings. Preserve the optimization-shape miss; no constant evaluator is supplied by the host.

This user class stores a deferred reader and has no one-argument constructor. Removing the lambda would change the API and fail; callee text alone cannot identify the Kotlin primitive array constructor.

limitations: The side-effect check is only body statement count, not effect analysis. Default-value checks are exact strings rather than constant evaluation.
Calls named IntArray can be user declarations. The shadowed constructor false positive remains an asserted upstream output, not suppressed or relabeled correct.
Two primitive families are authored here; this is not exhaustive testing of every signed/unsigned, floating-point or Char spelling in the upstream table.
No allocation/performance measurement, Kotlin type-checking, compiler-compatibility or optimization-equivalence qualification is claimed.
